questions.title: Trigger Definition
questions.description: What is a database trigger?
questions.Option2: A named set of actions that runs automatically when a specified event happens on a table

questions.title: Trigger Timing Options
questions.description: Which timing options can a trigger on a SQLite TABLE use?
questions.Option4: BEFORE or AFTER (INSTEAD OF exists for views)

questions.title: Trigger Events
questions.description: Which events can fire a trigger in SQLite?

questions.title: NEW on Insert
questions.description: In the snippet's trigger body, what does NEW.quantity refer to?
questions.Option1: The quantity of the row just inserted

questions.title: OLD on Delete
questions.description: When the snippet's DELETE runs, which values land in audit_log?
questions.Option4: The deleted row's sku and quantity, via OLD

questions.title: Trigger Body Delimiters
questions.description: How are the statements of a SQLite trigger body wrapped?

questions.title: Simple Audit Trigger
questions.description: No other triggers exist and audit_log is empty. How many audit_log rows does the snippet's UPDATE produce?
questions.Option1: 1 — one audit row for the one updated row

questions.title: Dropping Triggers
questions.description: Which statement removes the trigger t_log?
questions.Option4: ALTER TABLE items DROP TRIGGER t_log;

questions.title: Scheduled Events in SQLite
questions.description: Does SQLite support scheduled events (like MySQL's CREATE EVENT)?
questions.Option1: Yes — CREATE EVENT is built in
questions.Option4: No — scheduling belongs to the application or OS

questions.title: Event Scheduling Workaround
questions.description: A team needs a nightly stock roll-up to run inside the database at 02:00. What does SQLite offer?
questions.Option1: CREATE EVENT rollup SCHEDULE '0 2 * * *' — built in
questions.Option2: Nothing built in — SQLite has no scheduler, so the application or OS (e.g. cron) triggers the job
questions.Option3: A special TIMER trigger declared on items
questions.Option4: Enabling WAL mode activates scheduled jobs

questions.title: WHEN Clause Purpose
questions.description: What does the WHEN clause on a trigger do?
questions.Option3: Limits firing to rows that satisfy the condition

questions.title: UPDATE OF Column Scope
questions.description: items holds id 1 with quantity 40. How many audit rows does the snippet's UPDATE produce?
questions.Option1: 0 — the SET list has no quantity, so an UPDATE OF quantity trigger does not fire
questions.Option4: An error — UPDATE OF cannot be combined with triggers

questions.title: BEFORE Use Case
questions.description: A BEFORE trigger is the natural place to…
questions.Option1: Log the outcome after the fact only
questions.Option2: Validate or adjust the row before the change lands

questions.title: Multiple Triggers Ordering
questions.description: Two row-level triggers are created for the same event on the same table. In what order do they fire in SQLite?
questions.Option4: In the order they were created, as each affected row is processed

questions.title: Guarded Trigger Count
questions.description: items holds id 6 (WH-3001, quantity 5) and id 5 (WH-2002, quantity 80). How many audit_log rows appear after both updates?
questions.Option1: 1 — only the low-stock row passes the WHEN clause

questions.title: RAISE in Triggers
questions.description: Inside a trigger body, what does RAISE(ABORT, 'msg') do?
questions.Option3: It aborts the triggering statement with the given error message

questions.title: NEW and OLD on DELETE
questions.description: In an AFTER DELETE trigger, which row references are valid?
questions.Option2: OLD only — the row is gone, so no NEW version exists
questions.Option4: Neither — DELETE triggers cannot reference rows

questions.title: Trigger on a View
questions.description: What does SQLite allow when you try to attach a trigger to a view?
questions.Option1: Regular BEFORE/AFTER triggers work like on tables
questions.Option4: Only INSTEAD OF triggers may be defined on views

questions.title: Cascade Timing
questions.description: What does the snippet's final SELECT print?
questions.Option3: before, after — the BEFORE trigger fires first for the row

questions.title: Why Audit Via Triggers
questions.description: Why put audit logging in triggers instead of application code?
questions.Option1: Every write path is captured consistently — even writes that bypass the application
questions.Option2: Triggers are always faster than application code
questions.Option3: Triggers replace the need for backups
